root_cause.text: In `drivers/power/supply/pm8916_lbc.c`, the driver requested the threaded IRQ with `devm_request_threaded_irq()` before allocating/registering the `extcon` device, so devm cleanup freed `chg->edev` before the IRQ handler was torn down, allowing an interrupt during removal to call `extcon_set_state_sync()` on a freed extcon handle.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `devm_request_threaded_irq(dev, irq, ..., chg)` from before `chg->edev = devm_extcon_dev_allocate(...)` / `devm_extcon_dev_register(...)` to after it, and the commit message explicitly states that devm deallocates in reverse order, creating a race where the IRQ handler can run after the extcon handle has been freed but before IRQ unregistration.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove premature IRQ registration from charger probe so interrupt setup is no longer performed at this stage.
intent_record.what: The probe function no longer requests the threaded IRQ immediately after validating the IRQ number; the `devm_request_threaded_irq()` call block for `pm8916_lbc_charger_state_changed_irq` has been removed from `pm8916_lbc_charger_probe()`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the driver will no longer register the charger state-changed interrupt handler at this point in probe, so that interrupt will not be enabled/handled from this code path during device initialization.

intent_record.intent_summary: Request the charger IRQ during probe so state changes are handled by the driver.
intent_record.what: In `pm8916_lbc_charger_probe()`, a new `devm_request_threaded_irq()` call was added after extcon registration to request the charger IRQ with `pm8916_lbc_charger_state_changed_irq` as the threaded handler, `NULL` as the primary handler, `IRQF_ONESHOT`, and the name `pm8916_lbc`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the driver now subscribes to the charger interrupt so state-change events can be handled asynchronously when the IRQ fires. This enables the driver to react to charger/USB state changes instead of only relying on probe-time status reads.

This is part of the premature threaded IRQ request that created the lifetime ordering bug between the IRQ handler and the extcon device.

vuln_statements.explanation: This threaded IRQ request was made before the extcon device was allocated and registered, creating the lifetime ordering bug that allowed cleanup to free chg->edev before the IRQ handler was torn down.
This completes the premature devm_request_threaded_irq() call that registered the interrupt handler too early, enabling the handler to race with removal and use a freed extcon handle.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable ordering is present in this probe function. The driver calls `devm_request_threaded_irq(dev, irq, NULL, pm8916_lbc_charger_state_changed_irq, IRQF_ONESHOT, "pm8916_lbc", chg);` very early, before the extcon device is allocated/registered. Only later does it do `chg->edev = devm_extcon_dev_allocate(dev, pm8916_lbc_charger_cable);` and `devm_extcon_dev_register(dev, chg->edev);`. The IRQ handler directly uses `extcon_set_state_sync(chg->edev, EXTCON_USB, chg->online);`, so if devm cleanup frees `chg->edev` before the threaded IRQ is fully torn down during removal, an interrupt can dereference the freed extcon handle. There is no fix here such as reordering initialization, disabling the IRQ before extcon cleanup, or otherwise guarding the handler, so `is_fixed` is false.
